chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from someone else, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hijjam, from Humran, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
The one in Ihram may wear trousers if he does not have a loincloth with him, and he may wear the two leather socks if he does not have shoes with him.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: State of consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What are the exceptions for wearing sewn clothing and footwear for a pilgrim in Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of necessity (darura) in Ihram regulations, allowing pilgrims to wear sewn garments like trousers or leather socks when traditional loose garments are unavailable. It reflects the practical flexibility within Shia fiqh, ensuring that the ritual remains accessible despite material constraints, while maintaining the core prohibition of covering the head and feet with standard shoes.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from someone else, from Aban, from Abdul Rahman, from Humran, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one in Ihraam can wear the trouser when there does not happen to be a loin cloth with him; and he can wear the two shoes when there does not happen to be any slippers with him’.
en.sarwar: 6. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama‘ah from more than one person from ‘Abd al-Rahman from Humran who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
One in the state of Ihram can wear trousers if one does not find loincloth and al-Khuffayn (shoes) if one cannot find Na’l (sandals). ‘“(Fatwa best explains this Hadith)
